claude_proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: No magic_item kind exists in UnitRecord. The current union is SpellRecord | ClassFeatureRecord | MasteryRecord. Magic items need a new top-level record type (UnitMetadata & { kind: 'magic_item'; requiresAttunement: boolean; mechanics: MagicItemMechanics }) before any encoding can proceed.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Weapon (Greatsword, Longsword, Rapier, Scimitar, or Shortsword), Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

claude_proposed_widenings.name: attack_proxy_family
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Dancing Sword creates an autonomous weapon proxy that flies, repositions, and attacks independently using the wielder's attack roll and ability modifier. It tracks a 4-attack budget before auto-returning. No existing mechanics family (ongoing_effect, activation, triggered_reaction, anchored_trigger, on_hit_trigger) can honestly represent: (a) an autonomous proxy making independent attacks, (b) a per-use countdown driving a forced lifecycle transition (return-to-hand), (c) repeatable Bonus-Action reposition+attack on subsequent turns. The v4 taxonomy has attack_proxy attachment and create_attack_proxy effect atoms, but no family wires them into a coherent subgraph.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: the weapon begins to hover, flies up to 30 feet, and attacks one creature of your choice within 5 feet of itself. The weapon uses your attack roll and adds your ability modifier to damage rolls. [...] After the hovering weapon attacks for the fourth time, it flies back to you

claude_proposed_widenings.name: attune procedure in surface types
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Attunement is a prerequisite for this item and is listed as a v4 atom ('attune') in TAXONOMY_atoms_graph.md, but there is no attunement_slot resource, no attune procedure, and no attunement_slot cap in types.ts. Any honest MagicItemRecord encoding needs attunement modeled at the surface.
